Executive Summary

At an Inflection Point

Stripe has established itself as the preeminent developer-first payment infrastructure company, processing $1.9 trillion in total payment volume (TPV) in 2025—a 34% year-over-year increase that dramatically outpaces legacy peers. Following its first profitable year in 2024 and a secondary tender offer valuing it at $159 billion (February 2026), Stripe sits at an inflection point: scaling profitability, diversifying beyond core payments, and positioning for what it calls the ‘AI-native financial stack.’

Despite no imminent IPO plans, Stripe’s competitive moat—developer experience, full-stack financial OS, and the Bridge stablecoin infrastructure—is widening against a fragmented set of public-market peers.

🎯
Market Position: ~22% online payment processing market share, second only to PayPal (43%), but growing 3–4x faster in TPV (+34% vs. PayPal’s +10%)
💰
Financial Scale: 2024 revenue of ~$5.1B (+28% YoY); 2025E ~$5.8B; Revenue Suite on track for $1B ARR by 2026
📈
Valuation Premium: ~31x revenue vs. Adyen at 20x, Block at 1.7x, PayPal at 1.9x—reflecting high-growth expectations and product breadth
🔧
Product Differentiation: Leads in developer API quality, billing/subscriptions, embedded finance, and stablecoin infrastructure
📊
Profitability Gap: Adyen operates at ~50% EBITDA margin vs. Stripe’s estimated ~18%—significant room to expand
🛡
Strategic Moats: 80% of top US software companies use Stripe; flywheel of developer adoption → enterprise expansion → multi-product attachment
⚠
Key Risks: Big Tech encroachment (Apple Pay, Google Pay), Adyen’s aggressive US push, regulatory risk on stablecoin infrastructure
I. Market Overview

A Once-in-a-Generation Structural Shift

The global payments industry is experiencing a once-in-a-generation structural shift. Digital payments now account for 66% of global e-commerce transaction value—up from 34% a decade ago—and 38% of in-store transactions. The total addressable market spans multiple layers: the payment processing solutions market was $173 billion in 2025 and is forecast to reach $1.05 trillion by 2035 (CAGR: 19.8%), while the broader digital payments transaction volume reached $18.7 trillion in 2024, projected to exceed $33 trillion by 2030.

  • E-commerce migration: Cross-border e-commerce growing at 16% CAGR, directly expanding Stripe’s serviceable market
  • Software-led payments: SaaS companies embedding financial services—Stripe’s core beachhead—now a $40B+ opportunity
  • Stablecoin adoption: USDC and stablecoin settlement volumes surging; Stripe’s Bridge acquisition positions it at the forefront
  • AI-native commerce: Agentic AI and autonomous purchasing requiring API-first, programmable payment rails
  • Instant payments: Real-time payment rail adoption (FedNow, RTP, SEPA Inst.) creating urgency for infrastructure upgrade
  • Emerging markets: India, Brazil, Southeast Asia mobile payment adoption creating greenfield international opportunities

II. Competitive Landscape

Market Share & Positioning

The online payment processing market remains highly concentrated at the top, with PayPal and Stripe collectively commanding over 65% of merchant adoption among online businesses. However, concentration metrics mask the qualitative divergence in strategy: PayPal is the consumer-wallet incumbent, Stripe is the developer-infrastructure leader, and Adyen is the enterprise-omnichannel specialist.

Figure 2: Online Payment Processing Market Share by Merchant Adoption (2025). Source: RedStagFulfillment, CoinLaw (Feb 2026)
III. Volume & Revenue

Total Payment Volume & Revenue Benchmarking

Stripe’s growth trajectory is the defining story of the modern payments industry. Processing $1.9 trillion in TPV in 2025—up 34% year-over-year—Stripe is growing at more than 3x the rate of PayPal (+10%) and meaningfully ahead of Adyen (+33%), while rapidly closing the absolute-volume gap with both. At current trajectories, Stripe may surpass PayPal’s TPV within 2–3 years.

Figure 3: Total Payment Volume ($T)—Stripe vs. Key Peers, 2022–2025. Source: PayPal 2025 Earnings; Stripe 2025 Annual Letter; Adyen 2024 AR

On a revenue basis, Stripe’s ~$5.1B (2024) positions it well above Adyen ($2.3B) but below PayPal ($31.8B) and Block ($22B). The comparison is imperfect—PayPal and Block include consumer-facing revenues and Bitcoin transactions, respectively—but Stripe’s 28% revenue growth meaningfully outpaces all public peers.

Figure 4: Revenue Comparison ($B)—Stripe vs. Public Peers, 2022–2024. Source: PayPal, Adyen, Block public filings; Stripe 2025 Annual Letter
IV. Competitor Profiles

Key Competitor Deep Dives

PayPal Holdings

NASDAQ: PYPL  •  Mkt Cap: ~$62B  •  2025 TPV: $1.68T (+10% YoY)  •  Revenue: ~$31.8B

PayPal retains the largest consumer payment network with 435 million active accounts, Venmo’s 90 million US users, and Mercado Pago’s dominant LatAm position. However, its checkout business faces structural headwinds from Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Stripe-powered checkout flows. CEO Alex Chriss is executing a ‘PayPal World’ strategy—interlinking PayPal, Venmo, Mercado Pago, WeChat Pay, and India’s UPI into a 2-billion-user network. Core weakness: lacks Stripe’s developer API mindshare and Adyen’s enterprise omnichannel capability. Trading at just 1.9x revenue, it is the most attractively valued but faces the steepest structural challenge.

Adyen N.V.

EURONEXT: ADYEN  •  Mkt Cap: ~$47B  •  2024 Net Revenue: $2.31B (+12.6% YoY)  •  EBITDA Margin: ~49%

Adyen is Stripe’s most formidable direct competitor in the enterprise B2B space. Purpose-built on a single global platform processing 150+ currencies and 200+ payment methods, Adyen excels at omnichannel commerce for large retailers (H&M, McDonald’s, eBay). Its ~50% EBITDA margin is extraordinary in fintech and reflects the discipline of interchange-plus pricing and minimal sales overhead. Strategic vulnerability: relative weakness in developer tooling and SMB/startup accessibility. Adyen is aggressively expanding its North American enterprise salesforce, a direct attack on Stripe’s growing enterprise customer base.

Block, Inc.

NYSE: SQ  •  Mkt Cap: ~$37B  •  Cash App MAUs: 58M  •  Square GPV Growth: +12% YoY (Q3 2025)

Block operates two distinct engines: Square (merchant POS and payments) and Cash App (consumer financial services). Square competes directly with Stripe in card-present and SMB payments, though its developer capabilities are materially inferior. Cash App, with 58 million MAUs and 24% gross profit growth, is Block’s crown jewel—effectively a neobank serving underbanked Americans with P2P, banking, Bitcoin, and investing services. Near-term headwind: gross revenue has declined YoY in recent quarters due to Bitcoin volume fluctuations.

Checkout.com

Private  •  Last Valuation: ~$11B (2022, down from $40B peak)  •  Focus: Enterprise digital commerce

Checkout.com positioned itself as the ‘Stripe for enterprise’ but has faced significant challenges, including a valuation markdown from $40B to ~$11B and leadership changes. It remains strong in regulated industries (crypto, forex, airline) with advanced fraud tools, but has lost ground to Stripe in developer mindshare and to Adyen in enterprise stickiness. Near-term strategic priority is profitability over growth—a contrast to Stripe’s reinvestment posture.

V. Product Capabilities

Competitive Positioning & Product Portfolio

Stripe’s strategic differentiation lies in the breadth and integration depth of its product portfolio—from core payment acceptance through financial operations (Billing, Tax, Connect) to banking infrastructure (Treasury, Issuing) and now stablecoin rails (Bridge). This ‘financial OS’ strategy creates multi-product lock-in that is qualitatively different from single-product processors.

Figure 5: Product Capability Matrix—Key Payment Processors. Assessment based on public product documentation and industry research (Feb 2026)

Payments API

Best-in-class REST API with 100+ payment methods, 135+ currencies, authorization boost AI, and lowest integration friction in the industry

Stripe Connect

Powers 20M+ platform businesses to embed payments; core infrastructure for Shopify, Lyft, DoorDash, Instacart

Revenue Suite

Programmable billing engine with usage-based pricing, automated global tax compliance (180+ jurisdictions), and revenue analytics

Stripe Radar

ML-powered fraud prevention processing 1T+ data points; recently opened via API for multi-processor setups

Issuing & Treasury

Banking-as-a-Service stack enabling platforms to issue cards and offer FDIC-insured accounts; powering neobanks and fintech startups

Bridge (Stablecoins)

Acquired Q1 2025; enables stablecoin-denominated payouts, cross-border settlement at near-zero cost; OCC trust charter application pending

VII. SWOT Analysis

Stripe Strategic Assessment

Figure 9: Stripe SWOT Analysis—February 2026. Source: Analyst assessment based on Stripe 2025 Annual Letter, FXCIntel, FintechwrapUp

Strengths — Deepening Moat

  • Developer flywheel: API-first approach captured 80% of top US software companies—self-reinforcing adoption cycle
  • Financial OS expansion: Every new product (Billing → Tax → Treasury → Issuing → Bridge) extends switching costs
  • Data network effects: 1T+ fraud signals through Radar create improving ML models competitors cannot replicate
  • Bridge/stablecoin first-mover: $1.1B acquisition positions Stripe as primary rails for stablecoin payment wave

Key Vulnerabilities

  • Pricing premium: 2.9% + $0.30 standard rate materially higher than Adyen’s interchange-plus model for high-volume merchants
  • Physical commerce gap: Minimal presence in physical retail POS—a $10T+ market dominated by Adyen, Block/Square, and Worldpay
  • Private market opacity: Lack of audited public financials constrains institutional diligence
  • No consumer identity: Unlike PayPal or Cash App, Stripe has no direct consumer relationship—entirely B2B2C

Strategic Opportunities

  • B2B/AP-AR automation: $120T B2B payments market largely untouched by modern APIs
  • Emerging markets: India, LatAm, Southeast Asia combined with Bridge stablecoin rails for remittance corridors
  • AI-native payments: Agentic AI systems require programmatic, API-native payment capabilities
  • Revenue Suite $1B milestone: SaaS-like recurring revenue driving structural margin improvement
  • Enterprise upmarket: AI-powered Authorization Boost addresses enterprise treasury pain points

Key Risks

  • Big Tech disintermediation: Apple Pay and Google Pay increasingly commoditizing checkout
  • Adyen US expansion: Aggressively hiring enterprise salespeople; recently won LVMH, Under Armour from Stripe
  • Regulatory risk on Bridge: OCC trust charter and stablecoin legislation create binary outcomes
  • IPO timing risk: Continued private status limits employee liquidity; talent attrition risk
  • Credit cycle sensitivity: Volume correlated with e-commerce and consumer spending

IX. Investment Thesis

Strategic Recommendations

Stripe represents the clearest long-term winner in the developer-first financial infrastructure category. Its combination of API quality, product breadth, network data, and the Bridge stablecoin platform creates a compounding competitive advantage that is extremely difficult to replicate. The thesis rests on three pillars:

01

Take-Rate Expansion

As Revenue Suite scales toward $1B ARR, the blended take rate on processed volume improves. Billing and Treasury products carry higher margins than raw payment processing, improving unit economics without volume growth.

02

Enterprise Upsell

2025 enterprise product launches (Auth Boost, Workflow/Script APIs, Adaptive Pricing) show deliberate upmarket movement. As enterprise accounts grow, ARPA expands and churn falls.

03

Stablecoin Platform

Bridge’s infrastructure for USDC-native payouts and treasury management could be a $5–10B opportunity over 5 years as stablecoin B2B settlement goes mainstream in cross-border corridors.

Audience Recommendation
Enterprise merchants ($100M+ volume) Benchmark Stripe vs. Adyen annually on total cost; Stripe’s flat rate likely uncompetitive above $500M TPV—consider hybrid or Adyen for in-person channels
SaaS & platform companies Default to Stripe Connect; switching cost analysis shows 18–24 month re-platforming effort—loyalty to Stripe’s ecosystem is rational
Pre-IPO investors (secondary) Stripe at $159B implies ~31x 2024 revenue; justified if 2026–2028 revenue CAGR of 25%+ continues and EBITDA margin expands to 25%+ over time
Adyen shareholders Adyen’s 50% EBITDA margin and profitable growth are undervalued at 20x revenue; US expansion is the key monitoring variable

Bottom Line: Stripe’s competitive position is strengthening, not weakening. The combination of profitability, product expansion, stablecoin infrastructure, and AI-native positioning makes it the structural winner of the next decade in developer-first financial services. The key watch item is an eventual IPO, which would provide public-market price discovery for what may be the most important private fintech company in the world.
